module: Traffic police logic: tracks vehicles with the 'police' role, handles pursuits (levels -1 to 3 depending on the offense score), arrest, evasion, release, roadblocks (vehicles and props), and the queue of random suspects. It relies on gameplay_traffic (traffic data, roles). A modder uses it to start or end a pursuit, set the pursuit variables or set up a roadblock.
usage:
gameplay_police.setPursuitVars({arrestTime = 3, evadeTime = 30})
gameplay_police.setupPursuitGameplay(suspectId, {policeId1, policeId2})
gameplay_police.setPursuitMode(2, suspectId)
local ok, isPolice = gameplay_police.isVehicleInPursuit(suspectId)
notes: Pursuit levels: -1 arrested (busted), 0 none, 1 to 3 levels; the mode is bounded by clamp(-1, 3). The level is triggered by pursuit.score against vars.scoreLevels (default {100, 500, 2000}).

Default pursuit variables (vars): scoreLevels, strictness 0.5, arrestTime 5, arrestRadius 20, evadeTime 45, evadeRadius 80, suspectFrequency 0.5, roadblockFrequency 0.5, useVisibility true, autoRelease true.
setPoliceVars/getPoliceVars and getPolice are aliases of setPursuitVars/getPursuitVars and getPoliceVehicles.
setPursuitVars(nil) or (false) resets the variables; a table is merged into the current variables.
The variables are reset at the end of the level (onClientEndMission); they are kept by onSerialize/onDeserialized.
The extension does nothing if M.enabled is false, if physics is disabled (be:getEnabled) or if traffic is not in the 'on' state.
The random suspect timer only advances if gameplay_traffic.getTrafficVars().enableRandomEvents is true and vars.suspectFrequency > 0.
Emitted hooks: onPursuitAction(id, 'start'|'arrest'|'evade'|'release', pursuit) and onPursuitModeUpdate(id, {mode}).

enabled.desc: If false, the police logic at runtime (onUpdate) is suspended. Is true by default.

onTrafficSpecialVehiclesProviders.desc: gameplay_traffic hook: registers the 'police' special vehicle provider (priority 10, at least 3 traffic vehicles in total, 25% of the total rounded up if options.police). The group comes from a group file (if options.autoLoadFromFile or the trafficSmartSelections setting), otherwise from trafficUtils.createPoliceGroup, otherwise from the fullsize/police.

checkRoadblock.desc: Indicates how many of the provided vehicles fit in the width of a roadblock (from shortest to longest, length = largest extent of the box, or the axis chosen by useLength).

useLength.desc: nil = best axis; true = Y extent; false = X extent.

returns.desc: Ids that fit in the roadblock (nil if vehIds is not a table).

placeRoadblock.desc: Places vehicles in a row across a road (centered on pos, spread over placeData.width), then teleports them with core_multiSpawn.placeGroup.

rot.desc: Orientation (the forward direction must follow the road).

placeData.desc: width (default 10 m), angle (degrees, default 0), centerAngle (angle of the center vehicle).

setupRoadblock.desc: Prepares and places a roadblock in front of the target. Chooses the active police vehicles, farther than activeDist and behind the origin, that can target targetId. Looks for a road point at spawnDist ahead, computes the road width, adjusts the angle randomly, puts the police in 'roadblock' action and also places props (propIds).

activeDist.desc: Radiating distance (default 100 m); 0 skips the distance and direction tests.

spawnDist.desc: Minimum placement distance (default 120 m); 0 forces placement at the origin.

returns.desc: {vehIds, propIds} of the placed elements; nil on failure.

setPropsActive.desc: Enables or disables all registered roadblock props; with reset, calls recovery.loadHome() on each.

reset.desc: true to return them to their original position.

insertProp.desc: Adds an object as a roadblock prop, if it exists, is not already a traffic vehicle and is not already registered.

removeProp.desc: Removes a prop from the roadblock list.

setPursuitVars.desc: Merges data into the pursuit variables; without a valid table (nil/false), resets them to default. Alias: setPoliceVars.

data.desc: Variables to change (scoreLevels, strictness, arrestTime, arrestRadius, evadeTime, evadeRadius, suspectFrequency, roadblockFrequency, useVisibility, autoRelease).

getPoliceVehicles.desc: Table of the traffic police vehicles, by vehicle id (gameplay_traffic data). Alias: getPolice.

getNearestPoliceVehicle.desc: Active police closest to the target, based on the distances cached in role.validTargets.

isVisible.desc: Keep only the police that see the target (ignored if vars.useVisibility is false).

returns.desc: Interactive distance (the police is facing forward).

isVehicleInPursuit.desc: Pursuit status of a traffic vehicle: for a police vehicle, true if it is pursuing (optionally targetId); for a suspect, true if pursuit.mode > 0.

targetId.desc: Filter on the pursued target (police only).

returns.desc: The vehicle is a police vehicle.

setPursuitMode.desc: Sets a target's pursuit mode: -1 arrested, 0 end, 1 to 3 level. Gives the target the suspect role (fleePolice action), updates the police (pursuitStart, pursuitEnd, resetAction) and the score, then emits onPursuitModeUpdate. When going from 0 to >0, emits onPursuitAction 'start'. Has no effect if the target is not traffic or has ignorePursuit.

policeIds.desc: Police concerned (default all; a single number is accepted).

setSuspect.desc: Sets a traffic vehicle to the 'suspect' role with the 'watchPolice' action (kept on role refresh).

setSuspectTimer.desc: Sets the delay before the next random suspect. With no argument: 120 * coef * (1 - suspectFrequency)^2 + 15 to 45 s; coef is 2, 1 after an arrest by the police player, 5 after an evasion.

time.desc: Delay in seconds; nil = automatic calculation.

arrestVehicle.desc: Immediately declares a vehicle arrested: optional messages (ticket or arrest, list of offenses), emits onPursuitAction 'arrest' then setPursuitMode(-1) for the police targeting it. Works as intended if the target has the suspect role.

evadeVehicle.desc: Immediately declares that a vehicle escaped the police: emits onPursuitAction 'evade' then setPursuitMode(0).

releaseVehicle.desc: Releases a vehicle after arrest: emits onPursuitAction 'release' and sets the pursuit mode back to 0. If the vehicle is not traffic, sends controller.setFreeze(0) to its VM.

showMessages.desc: Show the "drive away" message if it is the player.

setupPursuitGameplay.desc: Prepares a pursuit scenario: inserts the suspect into traffic (without deactivation by the vehicle pool), disables its respawn, gives it the suspect role (pursuitMode), forces the 'police' role on the provided policeIds, and starts the 'watchPolice' action unless preventAutoStart.

returns.desc: false if the suspect is not found or if there is no police.

getPursuitData.desc: Pursuit data (veh.pursuit) of a traffic vehicle. Kept for compatibility.

onTrafficAction.desc: Traffic hook: tracks role changes ('changeRole' action) to add or remove a vehicle from the police list.

onTrafficVehicleAdded.desc: Hook: adds the vehicle to the police list if its role is 'police'.

onTrafficVehicleRemoved.desc: Hook: removes the vehicle from the police list.

onTrafficStarted.desc: Hook at traffic start: logs the number of police vehicles and props.

onTrafficStopped.desc: Hook at traffic stop: clears the police list.

onVehicleSwitched.desc: Controlled vehicle change hook: inserts the new vehicle into traffic if needed; on a switch on foot/in vehicle (jbeam 'unicycle') during a pursuit, transfers the pursuit data to the new vehicle, restarts the mode, and forces the arrest on a return to a vehicle in front of the police. Sets ignorePolice to avoid the self-arrest of a police officer getting out.

onVehicleResetted.desc: AI vehicle reset hook: optionally picks a random suspect among the 'standard' vehicles when the timer has elapsed, or returns a non-'wanted' suspect to the standard role.

onVehicleDestroyed.desc: Hook: removes the destroyed object from the props list.

onClientEndMission.desc: Level end hook: clears the police list and resets the pursuit variables.

onUpdate.desc: Called every frame. For each traffic vehicle, triggers setPursuitMode when the score reaches a new scoreLevels step (with a short delay at the start). Also handles the random suspect timer.

onSerialize.desc: Hook before Lua reload: returns {vars, propIds} and clears the police list (rebuilt afterwards).

onDeserialized.desc: Hook after Lua reload: restores vars and policePropIds.
